Yinquan / Lingyuk (Y26 → R86)

Region (English scoring-table division): Haless.

1444 starting country: Yinquan (Y26) Later formable country: Lingyuk (R86)

Conclusion in one sentence: Yinquan is a very long campaign that begins as a hot-spring, fox-spirit, and Maiden republic and ends in spirit-world ascendance and theocratic revolution: its cute, exploratory opening turns the ideal of human-spirit coexistence into a bloody utopia of class purges and forced remaking of Haless.

Story: very high｜Mission-tree length: very long (51 direct missions)｜Mission-tree update: local files updated through 7 September 2026｜Distinctiveness: extremely high｜Waiting burden: high｜Early pressure: medium-high｜Expansion capacity: extremely high

Identity and history

Yinquan (Y26) is a Gankin republic in northern Yanshen. In 1444 it has an oligarchic republic, follows the Accretive Path, and has its capital at Tsingchunquan. Its ruler, Holi Leng, is a powerful and highly unevenly skilled mage, especially talented in illusion, enchantment, and summoning; the country history also gives her Huli-Jing patronage.【Local history script】【Local localisation】

Yinquan was not always independent. The mission narrative says it belonged to the present sister country before the Ashen Sky, when the relationship was mother and daughter and became “sisters” only after independence. The Mulim was the traditional home of Yinquan’s people, but the Divine Empire’s division took half of it away. Older material describes the Yinquan people as refugees from the Bitter Sea who settled in the Mulim after the Ashen Sky. The current script confirms the 1444 identity around lost land, the sister relationship, hot-spring sanctuaries, and fox-spirit tradition.【Local mission text】【Older supplementary material】

The offline Wiki lists Yinquan as a Yanshen state with capital Tsingchunquan and ruler Holi Leng, and treats the Rending of Realms as the defining event of its era. Holi’s page describes her as one personality of the Huli-Jing Great Spirit who becomes Huszien’s dominant personality after the reformation. The country page is a stub; the current local scripts control the detailed route.【Wiki source】

National story and campaign line

The first half resembles warm folk fantasy. Recover the Mulim, unify northern Yanshen, rebuild relations with the sister country, and turn hot springs, rice wine, shrines, and pilgrims into a national identity. Meanwhile Liho’s Maidens enter every layer of government, and Yinquan changes from an oligarchic republic into a theocracy led by Maidens. Holi leaves court to travel Haless and investigate the High Temples, spirit fragments, and her own identity.【Local missions】【Local events】

The decisive turn is “The Saviour Reborn”. By investigating the High Temples and reuniting Huli-Jing and Gumiho fragments, Yinquan brings the ancient Great Spirit Huszien back into the world. If the global Rending has not begun, the mission sets an early-start flag and triggers the starting event one day later. The offline Wiki places the setting’s Rending around 1751–1783; that is a world-history date, not a fixed player completion year. Yinquan follows the special route of deliberately bringing the Rending forward, opening the later Maiden reconstruction of order.【Local mission】【Wiki source】

Afterwards, negotiate with Great Spirits one by one, complete their demands, choose the Mystic Accord’s appeasement route, and unlock spirit armies. Huszien eventually joins with Yanhe, stabilising the fractured spirit and presenting Yanshen’s unification as a sacred marriage. Completing the Sacred Fox Wedding forms Lingyuk (R86), but this does not start a separate tree: the later missions still accept a country that was formerly Y26 and has unlocked Huszien, so all 51 direct missions remain one continuous campaign.【Local formation decision】【Local missions】

After Lingyuk forms, the fairy tale changes completely. Liho’s Maidens monopolise power, beginning with land nationalisation and redistribution, then encouraging the massacre of urban merchants, pre-emptive purges of generals, and purges of bureaucrats. They use the Empty Mother to damage Xia, destroy High Philosophical Temples, kill scholars, and demand that conquest and forced submission bring Haless into spirit order. The final events describe disobedient Goblins, Harpies, and Ogres as obstacles to be eliminated.【Local missions】【Local events】

Core mechanics

Huszien’s revival and the early Rending. Yinquan does not passively await the Rending: High-Temple investigation and the assembly of spirit fragments trigger it deliberately. Huszien’s revival, spirit manifestation, and country transformation are one causal chain.【Local missions】【Local decisions】

Great Spirit appeasement and spirit armies. The middle and late game completes multiple Great Spirit demands, follows the Mystic Accord appeasement route, and unlocks spirit armies. Some requests require waiting, diplomacy, or temporary occupation of a specified site, producing a strong world-quest feeling and potentially interrupting expansion.【Local missions】【Official development material】【Community views】

Hot springs, shrines, and pilgrimage economy. Early construction is not merely development stacking: ten-thousand shrines, rice wine, hot springs, and pilgrimage income create a distinct folk-management phase before the turn toward violence.【Local missions】

Maiden theocratic revolution. Liho’s Maidens change from infiltrators into the only legal political class. Land reform damages the old nobility and redistributes land, but the same line forcibly purges merchants, officers, bureaucrats, and scholars. This is the mission tree’s national route, not an ignorable side evil.【Local events】【Local missions】

Continuous Tag conversion. The Sacred Fox Wedding lets Y26 form R86, swap ideas and missions, and continue through historical-Tag conditions. The deterministic index counts 51 direct missions in the Y26 file and no separately named R86 mission entities: one cross-Tag tree, not a contentless Lingyuk.【Local script】【Structured index】

Staged play

Opening integration: Recover the Mulim, manage the sister-country relationship, and control northern Yanhe and key Tianlou areas. Neighbours and territorial missions quickly force war, while hot springs, rice wine, and pilgrimage construction support the economy.

Holi and the fox spirits: Follow travel and investigation events, establish Holi’s nature, gather spirit fragments, and advance Huszien’s revival. Missions, events, and decisions are deeply nested; missing a prerequisite creates waiting.

The Rending and the Mystic Accord: Prepare the early Rending after Huszien’s revival, then appease Great Spirits. Preserve diplomatic, economic, and mobility capacity instead of advancing only by claims.

Lingyuk revolution: After forming R86, continue the same tree while expanding rapidly and rebuilding land, army, bureaucracy, and religious order. The military and map goals are powerful, but political purges are unavoidable.

Perfect Harmony endgame: Appease every Great Spirit and control broad areas of Yanshen, Rahen, and Vímdaal. This is not a small country’s identity mystery; it is an attempt to rewrite a continent as one human-spirit state.

Formable country and endgame

Lingyuk requires the Sacred Fox Wedding and the Rending to have reached the Great Awakening. The decision changes Y26 to R86, swaps ideas and missions, unlocks Huszien’s special aspect, and grants centralisation. Because the mission group accepts a country that was formerly Y26, the two Tags are one entry and one continuous campaign.【Local formation decision】【Local missions】

The endgame slogan is “Perfect Harmony”: every Great Spirit is appeased and humans and spirits are placed in one state without the old boundaries. The route supplied by the tree is not tolerant negotiation but conquest, forced conversion, class purges, and destruction of resisting groups. Lingyuk therefore actively turns a utopian vision into state violence.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 92/100｜Autocracy 75/100｜Magic↔Artifice 100/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 100/100)｜Pluralism 55/100. The stage profile is Yinquan (Autocracy 35, Pluralism 80) → Lingyuk (Autocracy 95, Pluralism 35).

The v2.1 value profile is neutral (50/100) with an escalating trajectory: Yinquan (good 78/100) → Lingyuk_transition (neutral 55/100) → Lingyuk_late (evil 25/100). Early spirit protection, coexistence, folk construction, and public reform are later joined by centralised power, political purges, forced unification, and extreme violence against groups refusing the new order. This is why the trajectory is described as escalating rather than as a static Evil label. The Chinese source repeats its phase comparison here: Yinquan (good 78/100) → Lingyuk_transition (neutral 55/100) → Lingyuk_late (evil 25/100).

Recommended for players who enjoy very long stories, fox-spirit folklore, magic and spirit mechanics, staged national transformation, and large-scale conquest. Avoid it if you expect a permanently cute fox nation or dislike waiting, province-specific objectives, cleansing narratives, and late continental expansion.

Community experience

One 2026 experience report found the first half engaging and the war against the Command tense, but noted that Great Spirit demands cannot be previewed, some require waiting or temporary occupation, and the later tree becomes conquest in every direction. Another post called the later sequence a “fox-demon cultural revolution” because of noble, merchant, general, and bureaucratic purges; discussion disagreed about whether the turn was sufficiently foreshadowed. These are player experiences, not replacements for the current scripts.【Community views】

Evidence boundary

This article concerns the local base Mod and localisation version v1.37.5.0, checked 23 September 2026. Tag identity, Chinese name, Y26 → R86 formation, 51 direct missions, 1444 identity, Rending trigger, Huszien route, Maiden purges, and endgame goals come from current local files.

The offline Wiki check covered Republic of Yinquan (page_id=4501, revision_id=31511), Holi Leng (4278/31810), and Rending of Realms (3278/32362). The Wiki's Rending chronology describes in-world history; the mission may allow the player to trigger it earlier, so these are not contradictory dates. The official development diaries, release context, developer replies and two player sources are catalogued in the source evidence; checked English chunks and translation limits are in the English translation receipt.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea groups are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven have been unlocked. Only national ideas themselves are listed: racial, government and mission rewards are excluded. A successor’s new set does not automatically stack with its predecessor’s ideas. Descriptions may recall history or portray future ideals, and do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Native English originals are reused rather than back-translating expanded Chinese localisation. Displayed effect values are inherited from the Chinese research data; any unresolved display units remain qualified, not silently corrected.

Yinquan (Y26) — Yinquan Ideas

Traditions: Yinquan Traditions

Effects: Diplomats: +1; Improve relations: +25%.

Idea 1: Land of Hot Springs

Throughout the woods and hills of Yinquan are countless warm and soothing hot springs which draw visitors from across Yanshen and beyond, as the aching folk of Haless, from peasants to nobles, come to relax in their healing waters.

Effects: National tax modifier: +15%.

Idea 2: Huli Jing Guardians

Our nation was founded by lost and destitute peasants who had left their hovels to find a better home. When they entered the Mulim, they were guided through its woods, and directed by the fox spirits known as Huli Jing to dig in specific areas, ultimately revealing the hot springs for which our land is widely known. Since then, the Huli Jing have protected Yinquan from the shadows, gathering around springs and shrines devoted to them, and many of our people keep foxes as pets out of respect for our trickster guardians.

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Idea 3: Taming the Mulim

The thick and confusing mists of the Mulim have confounded armies for eons, even restricting navigation by magical means. Our people have been embraced by the woods though, and quickly learned how to traverse the Mulim with ease. Some have even learned how to gather and harness the mists to shield our soldiers when on the march.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%.

Idea 4: Liho's Maidens

Liho was the most influential of the Huli Jing in guiding our nation in its early years, and it is said that she continues to live among us, leading us even now. Liho's Maidens are her closest and most devout followers, performing rituals and performances across Yinquan and diligently maintaining the countless shrines dotted throughout the Mulim.

Effects: Religious unity: +25%.

Idea 5: Conqueror's Spring

Harimar had heard of the springs of Yinquan long before he ever even entered Yanshen, and when he reached us he visited the largest of them all, enjoying himself to such an extent that he left a garrison of his warriors to defend it to ensure he could visit in perpetuity. More than a thousand years later, the same spring would be visited by the Phoenix Emperor himself, Jaher, and the prestige of the area, now known as Conqueror's Spring, increased even further.

Effects: Prestige: +1; Monthly splendor: +1.

Idea 6: Soaked Men Tell No Lies

The waters of Yinquan are known to loosen more than tired muscles - officials from neighboring lands tend to speak far more openly in our baths than they would normally, and we have eyes and ears willing to pass information along to our leaders.

Effects: Spy network construction: +20%.

Idea 7: Center of Neutrality

While Yanshen burns under the heels of warlords and conquerors, Yinquan has always been a land of peace and tranquility, where merchants of even warring nations can relax and trade in peace. We benefit from this serene atmosphere, finding lucrative trade opportunities from our visitors.

Effects: Global trade power: +10%.

Ambition: Yinquan Ambition

Effects: Free diplomatic policies: +1.

Lingyuk (R86) — Lingyuk Ideas

Traditions: Lingyuk Traditions

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%; Diplomatic reputation: +100%.

Idea 1: The Land of Ten Thousand Shrines

While initially a title dedicated to the Mulim forest, where it is said that shrines outnumber the trees, Lingyuk has earned the epithet "Land of Ten-Thousand Shrines". Encouraged by the spirit-revering government, shrines of countless kinds have popped up across Haless. Dedicated to all manner of spirits big and small (especially the Huli-Jing), the Mystic Accord has rocketed upwards in popularity - almost as if the people of Haless were waiting for the moment to proclaim their true faith!

Effects: Missionaries: +1; Missionary strength: +1%.

Idea 2: Huszien, Our Shepherd

All spirits are revered as protectors and mentors, but none more so than Huszien Herself. Already the leader of Yinquan, the realm which finally took up the mantle of uniting spirit-kind, She was a natural candidate to lead all of Lingyuk. Her reconstructed form is a veritable wellspring of magic; wed to Yanhe, She has at Her disposal an almost inconceivable amount of power. Huszien is loath to use it. After all, She does not need magic to steer the nation to greatness. When She does use it, however, even the mountains bend to the decrees of Lingyuk.

Effects: All power costs: -5%.

Idea 3: The Endless Debate

Huszien might rule the nation, but Her composite spirits rule Her. The Huli-Jing and the Gumiho, the aspects of Her existence, regularly gather together to debate how best to process the world around Huszien. This is known as the Endless Debate. Whoever is dominant in these debates influences Huszien's personality, advising Her to act one way or another even as she comes to her own conclusions. A unique arrangement like this has given Huszien and the ruling class a number of very important lessons on how to reach a consensus. Using those lessons, more minority groups can be placated without compromising the unity of Lingyuk.

Effects: Number of accepted cultures: +2.

Idea 4: Proclamation of Lingyuk

Haless has been forced away from its natural state for millennia. The High Temples, constructed by some loathsome batch of precursors, all but banished spiritkind from the continent. Separated from our brethren for so long, we have all but forgotten the truth of this land.

Nevermore! Lingyuk, the spirit domain, shall excise the rot that has set in; we declare war against all the false "nations" of Haless. Once their divisions have been washed away with blood, the continent shall return to the state it should have always been in: Man and spirit, co-existing in eternal harmony.

Effects: Warscore cost against other religions: -10%; Manpower from true-faith provinces: +15%.

Idea 5: The Maiden Enlightenment

The Maidens of Liho are an organization that dates back centuries. First patronized by Yinquan, they have since grown to encompass the entirety of Lingyuk's state. They practice a unique style of magic that makes heavy use of ritualized dances and the now well-known gohei staff. This magic serves to purify our weapons, ensuring that they always strike true. Our armor, meanwhile, seems all the more willing to suffer otherwise destructive blows after being imbued with Huszien's power.

Effects: shock_damage_received：-5%; Infantry combat ability: +5%.

Idea 6: The Flow of the Yanhe

Second only to Huszien is Yanhe, the Great Dragon. As he is the husband of Huszien, it is his duty to ensure that Her children are as well cared for as his. In this regard, Yanhe is generous; The Yanhe river is always welcome and friendly to the children of Lingyuk. Its waters are especially fertile, quick to rejuvenate the soil along its bank. Our farmers are able to produce great harvests with no extra effort - all through our harmony with the spirits.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +5%; Production efficiency: +5%.

Idea 7: The Land of Festivals

Yinquan's rich history of festivals, encouraged by the Huli-Jing, has proven contagious. Many of their holidays and celebrations have spread throughout Lingyuk, leading ultimately to the creation of a single, unified calendar. These celebrations are incredibly frequent, and during them men and spirit mix without any care for the identity of others. It is here that the harmony of Lingyuk can be seen in full display. All of the merriment has led to a much happier populace, too.

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Ambition: Lingyuk Ambition

Effects: Governing capacity modifier: +10%.
